note: THE APPEARANCE SPEC IS CANON, AND IT IS READ BY THE BUILD -- not documentation. Every material the rig creates comes from here, so a look cannot drift by someone editing a hex value inside a Blender script.

canonical.premise: MARS IS A FLOATING-HEAD BEING. The absence of a body is intentional character design, not missing geometry. Never invent a torso, never treat the neck termination as a defect, never regenerate the head.

eyes.why: HIS EYES ARE WHITE ON PURPOSE. No iris, no pupil, no visible gaze target -- that is the character, not a missing feature. A build that helpfully adds a blue iris because the donor mesh has one has redesigned him.
eyes.rule: The GNM donor eyeball ships sclera / iris / pupil as separate vertex classes. In the canonical variant ALL THREE take the sclera material, so the eye reads as one luminous white form while the geometry underneath stays capable of a pupil the moment a scene wants one.
eyes.noSocket: The reference shows NO socket, NO lid line and NO dark rim -- the eye is one luminous white shape running to the lid edges. So the socket behind the globe takes the SCLERA material: any sliver the globe does not cover reads as more eye, never as a wound. A dark crescent under the eye is a defect.

skin.rule: never replaced; shot looks are lighting and grade, not a new skin

reference.rule: This is the look. Every material here is measured FROM it, not chosen to match a memory of it.

measured.note: The reference shows NO eye socket, NO lid line and NO dark rim. The eye is ONE luminous white shape running to the lid edges. Any dark crescent around the globe is a defect, not shading.

canonical.label: MARS as written — solid white luminous eyes

pupils.label: Pupils visible — for a scene that calls for a readable gaze

human_skin.label: Human skin tone — for a scene outside the neon-blue look

SOCKET._why: THE SOCKET IS NOT THE EYE. This was an exact copy of SCLERA -- baseColor 0.93/0.96/1.0 AND emission 0.55/0.74/1.0 at strength 1.6 -- so every sliver of socket tunnel visible through the aperture rendered as a glowing white patch indistinguishable from the eyeball. That is what made the eyes read oversized and round at rest, and it is the white still showing under a closed lid: not the lid, not the texture, the lit socket behind it. HIS EYES ARE WHITE ON PURPOSE; the hole behind them is not. A near-black cool neutral, unlit, reads as the shadow an eye socket actually is -- which is what this file's own code comment said it was doing all along.
